get.summary: Get a consumer's administrative profile and resource history
get.description: Requires read:consumers in the Bearer JWT. Returns the current profile, global unfiltered resource counts and a bounded filtered page containing each job request, service proposal and work order as its own resource. This is resource history, not reconstructed event history. Current profile address and coverage zone are not attributed to historical resources. All profile, count and page sources use one consistent read-only snapshot per request. Before delivery, one access/prepared audit event is persisted for consumer/ID with the authenticated operator and effective correlation; it contains no profile/history content and requires no manual reason. Prepared does not prove client receipt. Required-source, public-photo resolution, operator-resolution or audit failures return an error without partial data. Operation detail, private chat and payments retain independent permissions and endpoint policies. Unknown, duplicated or empty query parameters are rejected. All route responses use Cache-Control: private, no-store.

Returns allowlisted audit-event metadata without exposing authentication credentials, external authentication identifiers, HTTP bodies, chat content, biometric data, or signed URLs. Requires the `read:admin_audit` permission in the Bearer JWT. Every accepted query is itself recorded as one prepared access event; the event is persisted before the response is released and is not included in that response. The response uses `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.
Filters are combined with AND. `occurred_from` is inclusive and `occurred_to` is exclusive; both accept RFC 3339 timestamps and are compared as UTC instants. Later events are excluded from subsequent pages, even if their occurrence timestamps would otherwise place them in the result. get.summary: Query the administrative hiring operations inbox
get.description:
Lists hiring operations across all users with a bounded summary. Requires the `read:admin_operations` permission in the Bearer JWT. Ordinary inbox queries are not recorded as audit events. The response never includes messages, chat excerpts, attachments, credentials, biometric data or payment payloads, and uses `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

**Operations.** A job request starts an operation that continues through the first service proposal of its conversation and that proposal's work order. Every later proposal in the same conversation starts its own operation, which references the same job request. Operations are never correlated by shared consumer, provider, email or time proximity, and payment attempts never add rows. The operation `id` is `jr-<job request ID>` or `sp-<service proposal ID>` and stays the same as the operation advances from request to proposal to work order.

**Stage** is the persisted status of the most advanced resource: `request_*`, `proposal_*` or `work_order_*`.

**Alerts** are derived at query time and never change persisted statuses:
- `request_pending_over_24h`: pending request created more than 24 hours ago (exactly 24 hours does not count).
- `booking_deadline_passed`: pending proposal whose booking payment deadline has been reached.
- `delayed`: scheduled work order whose scheduled time plus estimated duration has passed without a completion report. It does not prove that the provider missed the job.
- `stalled`: pending request, pending proposal or work order awaiting payment whose last business advance is more than 72 hours old.

**Last business advance** is the request creation (pending request), the proposal creation (proposal stages), the order acceptance (scheduled order), the completion report (awaiting payment) or the balance payment (paid). Messages never count. Job requests do not record their acceptance time, so an accepted request without proposals reports `null` with the `request_acceptance_time_unavailable` limitation and is never `stalled`.

**Filters** combine with AND. `started_from` is inclusive and `started_to` is exclusive over the operation start (request or proposal creation); both require RFC 3339 timestamps with an explicit offset (encode `+` as `%2B`). `scheduled_date` is a calendar day in `America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires` and matches work orders scheduled on it. Operations are ordered by start descending, then by `id` kind and numeric part descending. The default page limit is 20 and the maximum is 100. `next_cursor` is opaque and bound to the filters and limit of the first page; when continuing, omit them or repeat the same values.

Requires the `read:admin_operations` permission. The first proposal belongs to its request's `jr-<id>` operation; later proposals use `sp-<id>`. Payment milestones and timeline are restricted to the selected operation, never its siblings. The request's source assessment is resolved by its persisted reference, not the conversation's latest assessment; the address is the consumer's current address, not a historical snapshot. Missing relations are null or empty rather than synthesized. No messages, chat excerpts, storage URLs, checkout URLs, credentials or provider payment payloads are returned. A prepared audit access event is saved before the detail is delivered; audit persistence failure returns 500 without partial detail. Responses use `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

get.summary: Get an audited page of an operation's private conversation
get.description: Requires `read:admin_chat_audit`, independently of `read:admin_operations`. Resolves the persisted work conversation and participants from a stable operation ID, never from a caller-selected conversation ID. The first proposal associated with a request remains in its jr operation; later proposals use sp identities and may share the same complete conversation. Messages are not attributed exclusively to the selected proposal. Every page requires authorization and the X-Audit-Reason header. The UI may ask for the reason once on entry and resend it automatically on each page. One access/prepared event is saved before delivery or generation of private attachment access URLs. Prepared does not prove client receipt. Audit failure returns 500 without messages or signed attachment access. Only attachments owned by delivered messages and their persisted sender are considered; confirmed/private/purpose media policy is enforced. No participant membership, conversation state or realtime subscription is changed. This is chronological keyset pagination, not a frozen snapshot. Unknown or duplicated query parameters are rejected. A GET body cannot supply the reason. All route responses use Cache-Control: private, no-store.

parameters.name: X-Audit-Reason

Unicode surrounding whitespace is trimmed; the result must be nonempty valid UTF-8, contain no Unicode control characters, and occupy 1–500 UTF-8 bytes. Do not include messages, credentials or signed URLs. OpenAPI maxLength counts characters, not trimmed UTF-8 bytes, so that runtime limit is documented here rather than represented as an inaccurate raw-header maxLength.

Binds version, stable operation, persisted conversation, limit and the last delivered created_on/message-ID ordering key. Integrity and the persisted association are checked again; it is not an authorization credential. Do not decode, edit or reuse it for another operation.

get.summary: Query payment intents and financial evidence for administration
get.description:
Lists payment intents across participants for authorized investigation. Requires a Bearer JWT with the `read:admin_payments` permission. This is a read-only lookup: it does not reconcile, edit, or transition payment, transaction, proposal, or order records. Each valid query is recorded through the administrative audit path before result data is delivered; if audit persistence fails, the endpoint returns a controlled `500` without returning payment data. Malformed queries are rejected with `400` before the audit event is prepared. Cache middleware sets `Cache-Control: private, no-store` before authorization and applies it to responses, including errors. This cross-participant administrative view does not replace or broaden the participant-scoped `GET /payment-intents/{id}` access contract.

**Identifiers and matching.** `payment_intent_id` is an exact canonical internal intent UUID. `external_reference` also accepts that exact canonical internal intent UUID: it is the UUID sent to Mercado Pago when creating checkout, and is not an external payment ID returned or persisted from Mercado Pago. `external_payment_id` matches the exact persisted processor payment ID (not a prefix). `service_proposal_id` is an exact positive internal proposal ID and returns each matching intent. Consumer and provider email filters are literal partial text searches, case insensitive; emails themselves are not included in result rows. All supplied filters are combined with AND.

**Purpose, status, and dates.** Purpose is `booking_deposit` (seña) or `service_balance` (saldo). The intent-status filter and response include the current states `requires_checkout`, `checkout_ready`, `processing`, `paid`, `rejected`, and `expired`, plus historical persisted states `cancelled`, `refunded`, `disputed`, and `payment_mismatch`. Supporting these historical values for retrieval/filtering does not add transitions to the current payment flow. `created_from` is inclusive and `created_to` is exclusive over the intent's persisted creation time, not transaction verification time. Both timestamps require RFC 3339 with an explicit offset; encode `+` as `%2B` in a URL.

**Financial fields.** Monetary values are persisted integer minor units (centavos) and retain their currencies; no float reconstruction, currency conversion, or current-percentage recalculation is performed. The contractual breakdown comes from persisted proposal/order terms. Nullable breakdown fields mean a coherent derivation was unavailable, not zero. `approved_amounts` is proposal/order-wide and repeated on each returned intent for that proposal/order, independent of page and filters; it is not a global total or merely the current intent's total. It counts each distinct persisted `(processor, external_payment_id)` approved transaction once, gross and grouped by currency, including anomalous amounts or currencies. It is neither net revenue nor settlement. An empty array means no approved transaction evidence is known. `pending_amount` is a nullable contractual position, not an attempt sum: it is null when no order exists, terms are invalid, or a coherent position is unavailable; a valid accepted order in scheduled/awaiting-payment state with a matching paid deposit reports its nominal contractual remainder, and a valid paid order reports zero. Anomalous gross approvals are not converted or subtracted from a differently denominated contractual balance. Anomaly flags expose discrepancies for investigation only; the read never corrects them. Processor fees and net settlement are null because that evidence is not persisted; null is not zero and does not establish that provider funds were settled.

**Pagination.** Results use keyset order by intent creation descending, then internal intent UUID descending. The default limit is 20 and maximum is 100. `next_cursor` is signed, opaque, and bound to the first page's filters and limit. When continuing, omit the filters/limit or repeat them exactly; changed or duplicated query parameters are invalid. The cursor provides deterministic keyset continuation, not a cross-request snapshot guarantee: concurrent data changes may affect later pages. Unknown, empty, duplicate, malformed, or incompatible query parameters return `400`.

get.summary: Get activity statistics for the authenticated provider
get.description:
Returns activity counts and value totals for the provider profile belonging to the authenticated user. This is a self-service read: the provider is resolved from the Bearer token; the request cannot select another provider and does not require an administrative permission. Only aggregate statistics are returned; consumer identities and conversation content are not included. The results, evolution buckets, optional comparison, and current pending counts are read from one consistent database snapshot. `Cache-Control: private, no-store` is applied to successful and error responses.
`from` and `to` must either both be supplied or both be omitted. Each supplied value is an RFC 3339 timestamp with an explicit UTC offset (including `Z`), interpreted as an instant. When a timestamp has a positive `+` offset, encode the plus sign as `%2B` in the query string. The interval includes `from` and excludes `to`. PresignFileRequest.description: Request a direct upload URL for a file that will later be associated with a business resource.

original_name.description: Original file name selected by the user.

mime_type.description: File MIME type. Profile photos accept image/jpeg, image/png, and image/webp; conversation audio accepts audio/webm; conversation videos accept video/mp4.

size_bytes.description: File size in bytes. Profile photos must not exceed 5 MB.

purpose.description: Intended business use for the file.

file_id.description: API file identifier to use when confirming the upload and associating the file.

key.description: Storage object key generated by the API.

upload_url.description: URL where the client uploads the file bytes directly.

headers.description: Headers the client must include when uploading the file bytes.

key.description: Storage object key returned by the presign endpoint.

mime_type.description: MIME type originally requested for the upload.

size_bytes.description: File size originally requested for the upload.

FileAudioMetadata.description: Metadata for a confirmed standalone audio file.

duration_seconds.description: Validated audio duration in whole seconds.

FileResponse.description: Confirmed file returned by the upload confirmation endpoint. Common file metadata is exposed at the top level, while media-specific metadata is nested under the matching variant.

url.description: Public URL for confirmed public files. Omitted for private files.

original_name.description: Original file name selected by the user.

mime_type.description: Validated MIME type of the confirmed file.

type.description: Media variant represented by the response.

FileVideoMetadata.description: Metadata for a confirmed video file.

audio_codec.description: Optional validated audio codec for the audio track embedded in the video.

duration_seconds.description: Validated video duration in whole seconds.

MessageImage.description: Private image attached to a conversation message.

url.description: Short-lived authorized download URL. Clients must treat it as opaque and temporary.

original_name.description: Original image name supplied by the sender.

MessageAudio.description: Confirmed private audio attached to a conversation message. The URL is scoped to an authorized conversation participant.

url.description: Private, time-limited URL for the authorized participant.

original_name.description: Original audio file name selected by the user.

duration_seconds.description: Validated duration rounded up to whole seconds.

MessageVideo.description: Confirmed private video attached to a conversation message. The URL is scoped to an authorized conversation participant.

url.description: Private, time-limited URL for the authorized participant.

original_name.description: Original video file name selected by the user.

audio_codec.description: Optional validated audio codec included in the video.

duration_seconds.description: Validated duration rounded up to whole seconds.

CreateJobRequestRequest.description: Payload accepted by POST /job-requests to create a job request and its linked pending conversation. The consumer is inferred from the authenticated JWT subject.

provider_id.description: Existing provider identifier selected by the consumer.

title.description: Required job request title. Must be non-empty after trimming.
title.example: Reparación de fuga en la cocina

description.example: Hola Ana, necesito reparar una fuga de agua en la cocina. ¿Podrías ayudarme esta semana?

image_file_ids.description: Optional confirmed private image file identifiers attached by the authenticated consumer. At most 3 images are accepted.

JobRequest.description: Job request created by a consumer and linked to a pending conversation.

conversation_id.description: Pending conversation linked to this job request.

title.example: Reparación de fuga en la cocina

description.description: Optional job request description. Empty when omitted.
description.example: Hola Ana, necesito reparar una fuga de agua en la cocina. ¿Podrías ayudarme esta semana?

images.description: Images attached to the job request with short-lived authorized URLs. Empty when no image was attached.

JobRequestSummary.description: Pending job request item returned for the authenticated user.

conversation_id.description: Pending conversation linked to this job request.

title.example: Reparación de fuga en la cocina

description.description: Optional job request description. Empty when omitted.
description.example: Hola Ana, necesito reparar una fuga de agua en la cocina. ¿Podrías ayudarme esta semana?

images.description: Images attached to the job request with short-lived authorized URLs. Empty when no image was attached.

JobRequestRequester.description: Person who created the job request.

SendMessageRequest.description: Payload accepted by POST /conversations/{conversationId}/messages. The sender is inferred from the authenticated JWT subject. A message may contain text and/or images, one confirmed audio file exclusively, or one confirmed video with optional text. Videos cannot be combined with images or audio.

content.description: Optional message text. Must be non-empty after trimming when no images are provided.
content.example: ¿El jueves por la mañana te queda cómodo para pasar a revisar el problema?

image_file_ids.description: Confirmed private conversation-image files uploaded by the authenticated sender.

audio_file_id.description: Confirmed private WebM/Opus audio file uploaded by the authenticated sender. It cannot be combined with text, images, or video.

video_file_id.description: Confirmed private MP4 video file uploaded by the authenticated sender. The video must use H.264, may contain AAC audio, may be combined with text, and cannot be combined with images or audio. Videos are limited to 120 seconds and 1920×1920 pixels.

CreateServiceProposalRequest.description: Payload accepted by POST /service-proposals. The provider is inferred from the authenticated JWT subject.

consumer_id.description: Consumer user id that will receive the proposal.

amount.description: Decimal amount in Argentine pesos. The API converts it to cents in the response.

scheduled_on.description: Proposed service date and time. Must be in the future.

description.description: Human-readable description of the proposed service.
description.example: Reparación de pérdida de agua en cocina con materiales incluidos.

ServiceProposal.description: Service proposal created by a provider for a consumer.

amount_cents.description: Provider's total service price expressed in cents, excluding the platform fee.

description.example: Reparación de pérdida de agua en cocina con materiales incluidos.

BookingTerms.description: Immutable booking terms captured when the service proposal is created. All amounts are expressed in the smallest currency unit.

booking_payment_deadline.description: Immutable deadline for paying the booking deposit, fixed 24 hours before the scheduled service.

WorkOrder.description: Work order detail created from an accepted service proposal.

WorkOrderSummary.description: Work order item returned for the authenticated user.

WorkOrderCompletionReportRequest.description: Evidence submitted by the assigned provider after completing a work order.

description.description: Description of the completed work. Whitespace-only values are rejected.

image_file_ids.description: Confirmed private completion-image file identifiers in display order.

WorkOrderCompletionReport.description: Completion evidence recorded for a work order.

WorkOrderCompletionImage.description: Private completion image exposed through a temporary URL.

WorkOrderReviewRequest.description: Review submitted by the consumer for a paid work order.

rating.description: Whole-number rating from one to five stars.

description.description: Optional review description. An omitted description is returned as an empty string.

WorkOrderReview.description: Consumer review attached to a paid work order.

CreateChatbotConversationRequest.description: Payload accepted by POST /chatbot/conversations. At least text or one image is required.

content.description: Optional consumer question or description of the home problem. Must be non-empty after trimming when no images are provided.
content.example: Hay agua acumulada dentro del mueble bajo mesada cada vez que uso la pileta.

image_file_ids.description: Confirmed private conversation-image files uploaded by the authenticated consumer for pre-diagnosis.

ChatbotConversationResponse.description: Chatbot conversation turn response, including the chatbot answer and AI-ranked providers selected from the diagnosed category and the authenticated consumer's active coverage zone when the diagnosis is concluded.

messages.description: Messages persisted for this chatbot turn.

ChatbotConversationDetail.description: Chatbot-specific conversation state shared by detail and turn responses.

title.example: Pérdida de agua en la cocina

recommended_providers.description: Providers selected by the AI ranker from the deterministic category and coverage-zone eligible candidates, in rank order.

ProblemAssessment.description: Frontend projection of the current structured home-problem assessment.

ChatbotConversationSummary.description: Chatbot conversation summary returned by GET /chatbot/conversations for the authenticated consumer.

title.description: Short title generated by the chatbot for the conversation.

updated_on.description: Last time the chatbot conversation changed.

SentMessage.description: Message created in a conversation by one of its participants.

sender_role.description: Role of the participant that sent the message.

Conversation.description: Conversation created for a provider work request.

category_name.description: Provider category display name. Present only when the counterpart is a provider.

profile_photo_url.description: Public provider profile photo URL. Present only when the counterpart is a provider.

sender_role.description: Role of the participant that sent the message.

content.example: Hola Juan, necesito reparar una pérdida de agua en la cocina. ¿Podrías ayudarme esta semana?

ConversationDetail.description: Conversation detail visible to one of its participants. Type-specific data is returned under either `work` or `chatbot` according to `type`.

ConversationMessage.description: Message included in a conversation detail response.

sender_role.description: Role of the participant that sent the message.

content.example: Hola Juan, necesito reparar una pérdida de agua en la cocina. ¿Podrías ayudarme esta semana?

message.description: Present in JWT middleware validation failures.

CurrentUserResponse.description: Complete authenticated profile discriminated by role.

BaseCurrentUserResponse.description: Information shared by every authenticated user profile.

calendar_connection_status.description: Current calendar authorization status for the authenticated user.

ConsumerCurrentUserResponse.description: Complete authenticated Consumer profile, including the service address visible only to its owner.

identity_verification_status.description: Current identity-verification status for the authenticated provider.

identity_verified_on.description: Timestamp at which the provider's identity was approved, or null when it is not approved.

CreateCategoryRequest.description: Payload accepted by POST /categories. The implementation trims surrounding whitespace from name before validation and duplicate checks.

name.description: Category display name. Must be non-empty after trimming. Duplicate detection uses a lowercase normalized version. Length is measured in Unicode characters after trimming.

normalized_name.description: Lowercase category name used by the server for duplicate checks.

CategoryListItem.description: Category list item returned by GET /categories. normalized_name is not included in list responses.

id.description: Stable internal coverage-zone identifier accepted by provider coverage operations.

CoverageZoneBoundary.description: Google Maps boundary representation used by the current CABA coverage catalog.

type.description: Boundary representation understood by the frontend.

place_id.description: Google Place ID used to select and style the corresponding boundary polygon.

amount_cents.description: Provider's total service price expressed in cents, excluding the platform fee.

RealtimeNotification.description: Notification payload sent through the realtime WebSocket channel.

resource_id.description: Identifier of the resource referenced by the notification.

estimated_duration_minutes.description: Estimated service duration in minutes when the notification references a service proposal.

read_at.description: Null when the notification has not been read.
